articles.title: Spain's Canary Islands flooded by thousands of migrants as country declares emergency
articles.summary: Spain's Canary Islands processed over 2,200 migrants in two days as violent protests over housing costs and skyrocketing rents erupted nationwide.
articles.body:
Thousands of migrants flooded Spain's Canary Islands this weekend as the nation's government remains under a migration emergency.

The Canary Islands have received the brunt of migration from West Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa in recent months. Authorities there processed over 2,200 migrants in just two days, all arriving in dinghies and makeshift boats.

One flotilla of 14 boats landed on the island of El Hierro carrying 1,324 people. The island's Spanish population is just 12,000.

The Spanish government declared an emergency over the archipelago last week. The latest surge comes just months after tens of thousands of migrants crossed into Spain's North African territory of Cueta in July.

The country also faced internal unrest this month after a general strike turned violent last week and rioters began clashing with police, setting fires and bashing storefronts in hotspots across the country.

Violent scenes unfolded in Barcelona , where some demonstrators vandalized stores along the city's popular Paseo de Gracia shopping boulevard, set small bonfires and launched fireworks at officers arriving in riot gear and armored vehicles.

The violence erupted as Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years, with workers demanding relief from skyrocketing rents and the rising cost of living.

Housing activists claimed 400,000 people marched through Barcelona, while city officials estimated attendance at 55,000. Government officials reported another 120,000 demonstrators gathered in Madrid despite heavy rain, The Associated Press reported.

The nationwide walkout disrupted public transportation, forced some businesses to close and blocked major roads. Police made arrests across the country, while officers used pepper spray against demonstrators in Madrid.

Both the migration and housing crises are expected to play a major role in Spain's Nov. 29 parliamentary elections.

Fox News' Jasmine Baehr and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

images.caption: One of the migrants rescued after a cayuco capsized on May 28, 2025, in El Hierro, Canary Islands, Spain. At least seven women have died, three of them minors, following the capsizing of a cayuco with 180 people on board as it entered the port of La Restinga.

articles.title: Arch Manning will participate in Texas' senior day festivities before Arkansas game
articles.summary: Manning is in his fourth season with the Longhorns.
articles.body:
Saturday's game against Arkansas could be Arch Manning's final home game as a Texas Longhorn.

Manning, a fourth-year player, is participating in the school's senior day festivities ahead of the game. When asked about it Monday, Manning had a straightforward answer.

"I'm a senior, so I'm doing it," he said via the AP.

However, Manning's senior day participation doesn't mean much. Even without the NCAA's new five-for-five rule, Manning would have the ability to return to school in 2027. While Manning is about to finish his fourth season of college football, he'd be able to play next year anyway if he chooses to eschew the NFL because he played in just two games as a redshirt in 2023.

Manning, who said he didn't want to discuss his future Monday, has three clear options next season. He can return to Texas, head to the NFL or transfer to another school. Manning's draft status will be fascinating after an uneven-at-times season. He threw three interceptions against LSU before throwing the game-winning touchdown pass. And his late interceptions against Oklahoma led to the Sooners' Red River Rivalry win.

Manning could still be a first-round pick. Especially in a quarterback class that doesn't have much clarity.

If he stays in school — whether at Texas or elsewhere — he'll probably be one of the highest-paid quarterbacks in the country. A Manning transfer would also likely be the most talked-about player move of the NIL era.

But that's an option that's not worth discussing seriously at the moment. A win Saturday almost ensures Texas will be in the College Football Playoff. And given the way that the 2026 season has unfolded, we aren't discounting Texas' title chances if it makes the 12-team field even if the Longhorns haven't consistently looked like a complete football team.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 11 Panic Meter: Trey McBride's ceiling will be limited if Cardinals' offense continues to struggle
articles.summary: Ray Garvin highlights the panic level for players and situations in fantasy football going into Week 11.
articles.body:
This week, I'm starting with the team that might surprise you — because I've reached the point where there's nothing left to panic about.

New England totaled 151 net yards in a 35-10 loss to Detroit. Drake Maye exited on the opening drive, and Tommy DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards in relief. The passing game already offered little margin for error.

The bigger concern is Maye's ankle injury. Reports have raised the possibility that he could miss the remainder of the season , and Mike Vrabel doesn't expect him to be available immediately after the Week 11 bye. A season-ending absence isn't confirmed, but the fantasy playoff implications are serious.

That brings us to A.J. Brown. He's dealing with injuries of his own, and the temptation will be to put him right back into lineups whenever he's cleared. The numbers don't support it. Brown has 11 catches for 128 yards and no touchdowns in four games with Maye. DeVito doesn't improve that outlook.

Hunter Henry has a slightly different argument. Tight end has been a difficult position all season, and an inexperienced quarterback leaning on a veteran tight end makes sense in theory. But Henry's two catches against Detroit both came on the opening drive with Maye. He didn't record a reception from DeVito. He's a desperation option.

So, are Maye and Brown droppable in seasonal redraft leagues?

Maye is approaching that point, if the injury timeline rules him out for the fantasy playoffs, particularly in leagues without an available IR spot. Brown is more dependent on league size and replacement options. In a standard 10- or 12-team league, moving on is reasonable if the waiver wire offers someone with a clearer path to usable production.

There's no obvious quarterback rescue coming for this passing game.

Panic Meter: NO PANIC. Expectations have already been reset. New England isn't an offense to chase for fantasy production until the situation changes.

Chris Olave, WR, New Orleans Saints — SOME PANIC

Four targets for Chris Olave against Carolina. That's the number that stands out.

He finished with three catches for 30 yards, just one week after catching seven passes for 98 yards on 12 targets against Cleveland. The Cleveland game broke a streak of three straight outings under 60 yards.

Meanwhile, Jordyn Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards. The question is how Tyler Shough is distributing the ball, not whether Tyson has taken over.

Olave had reached double-digit targets in six of his first eight games. That volume helped offset the inconsistency of the Saints' passing attack and gave him a dependable path to fantasy points, even when the offense struggled. Fewer targets would widen his weekly range of outcomes.

One week doesn't establish a permanent shift, but Tyson's involvement is worth tracking. New Orleans doesn't consistently generate enough passing production to make an unexpected four-target afternoon easy to absorb.

Olave should remain in starting lineups. He still has the ability to produce strong fantasy weeks, and a single low-volume performance doesn't outweigh his season-long role.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC. The concern isn't Olave's talent. It's whether the target advantage that has supported his production is becoming less reliable.

Kyren Williams, RB, Los Angeles Rams — SOME PANIC+

If you've watched the Rams' backfield recently, Blake Corum's explosiveness has been difficult to miss. Sean McVay has noticed too, praising Corum's twitch and explosiveness after his 100-yard performance against Arizona.

From Weeks 8 through 10, Corum rushed for 231 yards on 39 carries, averaging 5.9 yards per attempt. Kyren Williams totaled 124 yards on 43 carries, just 2.9 per attempt. Corum generated nearly twice the yardage on fewer opportunities.

Against Arizona, Corum finished with 100 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. Williams managed 23 rushing yards on 12 attempts. The Rams won comfortably, but the backs had very different afternoons.

Williams still matters to this offense. His work in pass protection and the passing game gives him a role that doesn't disappear just because Corum has been more efficient on the ground. The question is how much of the rushing workload he can retain while Corum keeps producing.

There's no confirmed depth-chart change, but the old workload assumptions deserve another look. Corum has given the coaching staff a reason to keep him involved.

The Week 11 bye gives Los Angeles time to evaluate its rotation. Watch the touch distribution coming out of it rather than assuming the old split automatically returns.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC+. Williams is still a viable fantasy starter, but his weekly ceiling is getting harder to project with Corum earning more work.

Sam LaPorta, TE, Detroit Lions — SOME PANIC

Detroit scored 35 points against New England, and Sam LaPorta caught one pass for 16 yards. That sums up the problem. The Lions offense can function at a high level without LaPorta making much of an impact in the box score.

Over his last four games, LaPorta has nine receptions for 99 yards and no touchdowns on 16 targets. The opportunities haven't been there. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown remain central to the offense, and Detroit has enough ways to score without featuring its tight end.

For fantasy managers, that leaves LaPorta heavily dependent on touchdowns. It's a difficult way to operate at an already volatile position, especially when he hasn't found the end zone in four straight games.

There are reasons to be patient. Detroit routinely creates scoring opportunities, so a usage increase could turn into a productive week quickly. The problem is identifying when that usage is actually coming.

LaPorta shouldn't be viewed as an unquestioned starter based only on the quality of his offense. Matchups and available alternatives matter more now than they did earlier in the season.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC. Detroit's scoring potential keeps the upside alive, but it hasn't protected LaPorta's weekly floor.

Trey McBride, TE, Arizona Cardinals — SOME PANIC

Trey McBride caught every pass thrown his way Sunday. There were only five.

He finished with five receptions for 37 yards against the Rams, but Arizona's overall performance tells the bigger story. The Cardinals ran 34 offensive plays, earned six first downs and failed on all six third-down attempts.

Carson Beck threw for 108 yards with two interceptions in his first NFL start. Arizona scored six points and has managed just nine over its last two games. That's not enough sustained offense to support reliable fantasy production, regardless of how good McBride is at earning targets.

When drives end after a few snaps, even a strong target share means limited opportunities. McBride didn't lose his role. Arizona simply couldn't keep its offense on the field.

Total Panic would be premature. Beck drew a difficult Rams matchup in his debut, and one start isn't enough to determine what the passing game will look like over the final stretch. Kansas City is next, so the evaluation won't get easier, but the rookie deserves another opportunity before his impact on McBride is treated as settled.

The comparison with LaPorta is useful. Detroit can score without feeding LaPorta. Arizona needs McBride involved, but its offense hasn't been able to sustain drives. Same position, very different paths to disappointing fantasy results.

McBride should remain in starting lineups. Very few tight ends combine his talent with his share of their team's passing opportunities. The production may be inconsistent until Arizona improves, but benching him would create a different kind of risk.

Panic Meter: SOME PANIC. Give Beck another start. If Arizona continues to struggle to move the chains, McBride's ceiling will be limited by the offense around him.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares you can trust in Week 11 lineups
articles.summary: Fantasy analyst Fred Zinkie highlights some backup RBs who could crack starting lineups in Week 11.
articles.body:
Let's take a look at the backup RBs who have a Yahoo roster rate under 60% and could help fantasy teams to victory in Week 11. Players are ranked in order of their Week 11 appeal, and their current roster rates are listed in parentheses.

Two things were clear when the 49ers hung 46 points on the Cowboys. First, Christian McCaffrey is at the top of his game and the clear focal point of the offense. Second, even with McCaffrey having a heavy workload, there is still room for Black to have a significant role. The rookie has logged at least 11 carries in each of the past three games and has found the end zone twice during that stretch. While San Francisco is set for a challenging Week 11 showdown with a stifling Vikings defense, there may be no stopping one of the hottest offenses in football. Black is a flex option each week and an RB2 option in a Week 11 schedule that includes six teams on a bye.

Gainwell went into the Bucs' bye week on a high note, having averaged 101 yards from scrimmage in the previous three games. The 27-year-old is clearly second fiddle to Bucky Irving, who has been one of the top fantasy assets this season. But there are plenty of carries to go around in Tampa's run-heavy offense that leads the NFL in yards on the ground. They will likely remain conservative with play-calling when they visit the high-octane Lions in Week 11.

Managers who dropped McGowan when Jonathan Taylor remained with the Colts past the trade deadline were surely second-guessing their decision when McGowan tallied 77 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in a Week 10 win over the Dolphins. While facing Miami is one of the easiest matchups, McGowan is far from a one-game wonder, having averaged 5.8 yards on 34 carries over the past four weeks. After trading their top receivers and watching Daniel Jones struggle throughout the season, the Colts could copy teams like the 49ers and Buccaneers by running their offense through multiple RBs.

The bad news: Kamara touched the ball just five times in a Week 10 loss to the Panthers. The good news: he turned those touches into two touchdowns. The 31-year-old will continue to have a role in the offense, as Travis Etienne Jr. and Audric Estimé did little with their Week 10 opportunities. Kamara is averaging three catches per game, which gives him additional value in PPR leagues for a possible Week 11 shootout in Chicago.

Woody Marks will miss Thursday Night Football after leaving the Week 10 loss to the Browns with a concussion. David Montgomery may be ready to return for a favorable matchup against the Colts, but he hasn't played since Oct. 11 and may not be ready for a heavy workload. The Texans are double-digit favorites against a defense that has been repeatedly burned by opposing RBs, and Houston could spend the fourth quarter grinding out rushing yards to put the game away. Demercado is a candidate to fill that role after tallying 13 carries in the past two weeks. And if Montgomery remains out, Demercado becomes the starter and jumps at least two spots higher on this list.

Derrick Henry may be reaching the end of his illustrious career. The future Hall of Famer averaged 1.0 yards per carry against a mediocre Chargers defense in Week 10, which was the fourth time in the past five weeks that his average per carry fell below 3.5. Hill has managed to break a couple long runs this season and is averaging 6.8 yards per carry. He has also caught at least three passes in each of his past five games, including a five-catch game in Week 10. Hill should remain involved in Week 11, when the Ravens face a Panthers defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to RBs.

Although he wasn't especially effective, Washington led the Raiders with 23 rushing yards in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. Starter Ashton Jeanty once again dominated receiving targets, while Washington has led the team in rushing yards in four of their past five games, and his 3.9 yards per carry this season tops Jeanty's 3.2 mark. Washington should earn 8-10 carries but a lack of passing-game involvement gives him a low ceiling for a challenging Week 11 matchup in Denver.

Anyone who has watched Saquon Barkley in recent weeks knows that he is not fully healthy. The generational talent lacks his usually explosive burst, and it doesn't help that the Eagles are missing multiple starters while sitting at 2-7. Bigsby is expected to return from injured reserve for a Week 11 matchup against the Steelers, and he should immediately slot ahead of Elijah Mitchell on the depth chart. Bigsby could get 5-10 carries in that game and is worth stashing in the event that the Eagles eventually shut Barkley down for their meaningless late-season games.

Bhayshul Tuten was used heavily in a 40-point explosion in Week 10, carrying the ball 26 times and catching three passes. Rodriguez had an especially quiet day, with five yards on four carries. Truthfully, if there were fewer than six teams on a bye in Week 11, he would likely fall off this list. But with a dearth of alternatives, he's a TD-dependent flex option in deep leagues for a challenging matchup against a Giants defense that has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

Davis has had almost no impact on Buffalo's offense this season, totaling just 92 total yards over nine games played. Most weeks, Ty Johnson would be the Bills backup who could dent deep-league rosters, as he has caught 18 passes for 214 yards. But the Bills are massive favorites for a Week 11 home game against the 1-8 Dolphins, with the point spread sitting around 16-17 points. If the team builds a massive lead, Davis is the most likely candidate to receive plenty of second-half carries.

The players listed below are unlikely to provide significant assistance in Week 10 but are an injury away from having significant value.

articles.title: In scathing rebuke of college sports, former Big 12 AD calls NIL system money laundering
articles.summary: Former Iowa State athletic director Jamie Pollard delivered a scorching appraisal of the world he recently left, predicting college sports could be triggerin...
articles.body:
Former Iowa State athletic director Jamie Pollard delivered a scorching appraisal of the world he recently left, predicting college sports could be triggering something akin to the country's "next savings-and-loan crisis" and equating the system that generates NIL payments to players as a money-laundering operation.

"Somehow we're taking money that was supposed to come to our institution and find a way for it to be not given to our institution so we can launder it and create a manufactured NIL deal," Pollard said Wednesday at a seminar held by the college watchdog Knight Commission.

He was referring to the practice many schools use when they work with third parties to broker NIL deals for players. Those deals are allowable constructs that let schools blow past the $21.5 million revenue-sharing cap set by the landmark House settlement that allows college athletes to be paid.

Since the onset of NIL, some sports-focused donations that, in the past, would have gone to an athletic department have been diverted to businesses closely affiliated to the schools. They, in turn, have negotiated the so-called third-party NIL contracts.

Pollard, who spent 21 years as the Cyclones AD before stepping down this fall, decried this process as creating a lack of transparency that "is fueling emotional and irrational decisions" made by schools and conferences.

While schools must report player contracts to the newly created College Sports Commission and the commission gives a broad-brush overview of how much money is spent , there's still very little verified information about how much each school spends on rosters or how much individual athletes make.

Without that transparency, a handful of schools are reportedly spending $50 million on football rosters to stay competitive.

"Those decisions are multiplying like rabbits," Pollard said. "We've created distrust within our industry, (among) our colleagues."

Pollard connects spending for sports to bigger problems ahead for schools

Pollard, whose Big 12 program was a steady presence at both men's and women's March Madness in basketball but rarely broke through in football, cited other research that showed about 16% of public universities lost money in at least five fiscal years between 2014-23. He cited spiraling expenses in sports as part of the reason.

A report this year from the U.S. Government Accountability Office found that 94% of NCAA Division I athletic programs spent more money than they generated in athletics revenue in 2023-24.

"If we're not careful, we're sitting on the next savings and loans crisis in higher education," Pollard said.

A combination of high interest rates and poor management led to the closure of more than 1,000 savings-and-loan institutions around the country in the late 1980s and early '90s.

Leaders from Ivy League, Towson echo concerns about spiraling spending

Other seminar speakers included Robin Harris, the executive director of the Ivy League, and Steve Eigenbrot, the athletic director at Towson, which plays in Division I's smaller-conference Football Championship Subdivision.

Harris lauded the Ivy League's efforts to stay relevant despite not tapping into revenue sharing models that all but about four dozen of the 365 schools in Division I have signed onto.

"The Ivy League remains even more committed to our model in the face of these external pressures," Harris said.

She said in light of the recent announcement of the College Football Playoff's upcoming expansion to 24 teams that "it is time for a meaningful examination of the CFP and FBS football's financial relationship with the NCAA, given the many services the NCAA provides FBS."

FBS is the Football Bowl Subdivision that includes the Power Four and Group of Six conferences — a total of 137 teams.

Eigenbrot questioned the legitimacy of the market college sports has established for its players.

He compared the $45,000 average salary of a player in the NBA's developmental G-League — considered an option for players who don't want to attend college — against the six and seven-figure payments that often go to college players.

"I'm not so sure that if we fast forward three, four, five years down the line, that we haven't done ourselves a disservice relative to the actual name, image and likeness value of an 18- to 22-year-old," Eigenbrot said.

articles.title: LSU coach Lane Kiffin can’t win big games, but he just stole a 4-star safety commit from Wake Forest
articles.summary: Even though Lane Kiffin is facing criticism after a disappointing season, the LSU head coach is still scoring touchdowns on the recruiting trail. The LSU fo...
articles.body:
Even though Lane Kiffin is facing criticism after a disappointing season, the LSU head coach is still scoring touchdowns on the recruiting trail. The LSU football program was able to flip a Wake Forest commit, per Rivals.

"Four-Star Safety Keland Shelton Jr. has Flipped his Commitment from Wake Forest to LSU," Hayes Fawcett reported on X, formerly Twitter. "The 6'2 200 (pound) safety had been committed to the Demon Deacons since May."

LSU's newest commit expressed his loyalty to the Tigers, after making the decision. He is a member of the Class of 2027. He also had offers from many other power 4 schools, including Virginia Tech and Tennessee.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"LSU Nation I am coming to give my all! GEAUX TIGERS," Shelton Jr. said, which was reported by Rivals.

LSU is hoping to finish the season on a high note

The LSU football program is 6-4 this season . This is Kiffin's first year in Baton Rouge. His LSU team has lost several close games, which effectively ended their shot at making the College Football Playoff this year.

"Three of LSU's losses (Ole Miss, Kentucky and Texas) were by a combined 10 points, so a different bounce here or there would have changed an outcome, like a receiver not falling on one of Sam Leavitt's interceptions against Texas or a tipped pass ending in a pick against Ole Miss," The Athletic reported.

The team's latest loss was to Texas. LSU was nipped by the Longhorns, 22-21.

"Everything isn't built for the first year when you come in somewhere," Kiffin said after the Texas loss.

It wasn't supposed to be like this though for the Tigers. Kiffin left his last job, Ole Miss, near the end of the 2025 season to come to Baton Rouge. His final Ole Miss team was headed to the CFP, and Kiffin decided to bolt even when he could have led that group to a national championship.

LSU fans expect Kiffin to take the Tigers to the CFP as soon as possible. He will now have to wait until the 2027 season to have another chance.

articles.title: The Revue: Skyfall
articles.summary: This is the end (?) Hold your breath and count to 10.
articles.body:
What's your favorite James Bond movie? Or maybe who's your favorite James Bond?

Personally, I'm a Daniel Craig absolutist. I think some of the early Connery films are pretty good – specifically Goldfinger – and Roger Moore certainly had his moments redefining the character as a Baby Boomer self-parody. But Craig is everything I want Bond to be. Charismatic, brooding, and skilled, with just enough darkness to never betray how jingoist the character is at heart. So maybe it's not a surprise that my favorite Bond film is the one largely viewed as the crowning glory of Craig's 007 run – Skyfall .

If you haven't seen Skyfall and you have even a modicum of interest in the James Bond character, I'd highly recommend it. Without getting too in the weeds of the plot, no film has ever done more to dissect the neuroses and character flaws that would make a person like James Bond the byproduct of a forgone age. Not only that, it leans fully into the anti-social characteristics of James Bond's character. Sure, he's still sleeping with dames and killing for king and country. But it's one of the rare Bonds where you really feel good about everything he's up to.

I also think Skyfall serves as an interesting referendum on the series more than 10 years removed from its production. Craig would go on to make two more tepidly-received Bond movies, and now the franchise is being handed to the capable talents of Denis Villeneuve and Robert Pattinson. Did I mention the Broccoli family, long-time family stewards of the Bond character, are no longer the sole owners and distributors of the franchise? That would be Amazon. Welcome to the 21st century, Mr. Bond.

At no point in the last 25 years has the James Bond character held more cultural sway than just after Skyfall was released. It was praised on not just the merits of a celebrated action blockbuster, but as a critically-acclaimed piece of political espionage craft. Since then, things have felt a little… boring. You know, like a British meal. And when that happens, producers shake things up. Recast. Bring in a new director. The works.

I may be overstating things – after all, it's not like Mizzou fans expected the Tigers to roll into Athens and put one on Georgia – but I'm starting to wonder when Mizzou's Skyfall happened under Eli Drinkwitz. And when might it be time to reimagine what this franchise can look like.

I want to be clear: I'm not advocating Eli Drinkwitz get the axe. If anything, I view Drink as the Broccoli family stand-in of this metaphor. He's been an excellent shepherd of the Mizzou brand since his arrival. He's steadied a program that was still wallowing the shadow of state funding cuts, the 2015 protests, and Gary Pinkel's legacy. He's raised the overall profile of the Tigers from SEC also-rans to perennial Top 25 program. When Drinkwitz took over, a .500 record was seen as the baseline. Ask a Mizzou fan how they'd feel about finishing 6-6 this season. Hope you like seeing a person's blood pressure rise!

But it's clear that Eli Drinkwitz's tenure at Mizzou is currently in something like a creative fallow period. Maybe it's Spectre and we've still got a ways to go before we tweak the right things to get a fresh start. Maybe this season is more of a No Time to Die scenario where we're seeing the quality rebound, but not enough to avoid major changes.

So what does that look like? Is it building next season's offense entirely around Austin Simmons and deprioritizing the outside zone game that allows Mizzou to control games, if not entirely dominate them? Maybe it's admitting that the Chip Lindsey hiring, novel as it seemed, might be a failed experiment. Maybe the changes are smaller, personnel-related tweaks that can be done mostly underneath the hood.

I also think there's a possibility that I'm over-egging the pudding here and that Mizzou hasn't reached a sort of nadir yet. When you look at the amount of players on this team that are eligible to return in 2027, it's hard not to view this season – at least in the hindsight that we have – similar to how we might have viewed 2006. The Tigers were good that year, but were really on the way to building something unforgettable in 2007. The talent is there, after all. The opportunity will be there too, with the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 entrants.

But there's a lot of time between now and then. There are still two games to play. And a whole lot of bad things can happen against Kentucky and an Oklahoma team that suddenly remembered how to play football.

So to quote Adele: "Let the sky fall. When it crumbles, we will stand tall and face it all together."

Except, you know… let's avoid any truly "sky is falling" moments if at all possible.

For losing to Georgia and making me think existentially for this column – always hate doing that – Mizzou gets 1/5 martinis . Shaken, not stirred, because James Bond is an alcoholic who doesn't make his drinks correctly.

images.caption: Look, I enjoy a wet martini myself, but why are we diluting the only ingredients of the drink?!

articles.title: Chennis Berry puts South Carolina State championship success into perspective
articles.summary: The Chennis Berry era at South Carolina State has been an unprecedented success. Heading into the final week of MEAC regular-season play, Berry has yet to lo...
articles.body:
The Chennis Berry era at South Carolina State has been an unprecedented success. Heading into the final week of MEAC regular-season play, Berry has yet to lose a conference game, has won his third straight MEAC championship, and is making his third straight appearance in the Cricket Celebration Bowl.

In recent comments to the media, Berry put his success into perspective, showing reverence to the legendary South Carolina State coaches who came before him. Asked how it feels to join those names with three straight MEAC titles, Berry called them living legends and said he can only be himself.

"Well, you're talking about some living legends, man, so I can't be them. I can only be Chennis Berry."

He said he has the opportunity to write his own story and build his own legacy.

"I get a chance, I got a pen, right? And on this pen, I get a chance to write my own story, build my own legacy. All in all, man, I'm grateful. I stand on the shoulders of giants, man. These are giants, man. I'm not just talking about in HBCU football, I'm talking about nationally."

Berry said he is grateful to be around the history of the program every day, naming Willie Jeffries, Oliver Buddy Pough and Bill Davis.

"I'm grateful to be able to come here every day and just hear those names: Willie Jeffries, Oliver Buddy Pough, Bill Davis. These are shoulders that I get a chance to stand on, man. But it's my opportunity, as the guy that's new here, to find a way to write my own story."

Berry added that the records and championships those coaches built are hard to catch up to, and that his focus stays on the present.

"They got so many records and so many championships, man. It's hard to catch up with them guys, man. So all in all, I just try to be the best I can be on this day. On November the 16th, 2026, I want to be the best Chennis Berry I can be and try to find a way to win this thing."

South Carolina State concludes the regular season hosting Delaware State, then are set to play the SWAC Champions in the Cricket Celebration Bowl.

articles.title: Jamie Carragher calls on Liverpool to back Andoni Iraola in January transfer window
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has called on the Liverpool hierarchy to back manager Andoni Iraola in the upcoming January transfer window, having identified two key positi...
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher is convinced Andoni Iraola must capitalize on the opportunity to utilize the January transfer window to remedy the holes in his Liverpool roster.

What's more, the Anfield icon believes the Reds manager would gain from a decisive win over fierce North West rivals Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday.

Iraola has presided over a consistent beginning to his Liverpool tenure after replacing the dismissed Arne Slot in June, with four senior players acquired for a combined sum exceeding £200 million ($364.2 million).

However, Carragher maintains there are still obvious areas requiring enhancement in the playing squad and that Liverpool must conduct business in the upcoming New Year market.

"I look at this January window for Andoni Iraola and think he needs to go and get the player he wants for the certain position rather than waiting for the summer," he said, via the Liverpool Echo .

"He's only signed a two-year contract, and that was of his own accord which is fine, but that means every transfer window is very important.

"For me, this season for Iraola is about making sure Liverpool are in a position for next season to really challenge for the title. So every transfer window is important.

"The areas on the pitch for Liverpool that still stand out for are the full-back areas. If there's a left-back, they've got to go and do it in January. Or a midfield player, a certain type of midfield player."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

Despite sitting fourth in the early Premier League standings, Liverpool have managed just five points from five home fixtures, extending a disappointing top-flight record at Anfield this calendar year.

United currently occupy the relegation zone and last week brought in Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach following Michael Carrick's dismissal, yet they have lost only one of their last seven encounters with Liverpool.

Regarding Iraola, Carragher - speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate - commented: "I think he's made a good start. The one thing lacking is a stellar performance.

"How big is the Manchester United game? For us (as players), obviously it was a big game, but also for the manager really because at the end of the day, if you're the manager of Liverpool, you're going to have to beat your rivals to get over the line in a cup final or a semi-final or win a league.

"And so far, even though the performances were good, I'd say against Manchester City when it was 11 v 11, and Arsenal in the main, both games at home, they lost both of them. Manchester United are coming to town, Liverpool's biggest rivals. I think the manager could do with winning a big home game."
